faq: Do you need my passwords to check security?
Never. You add us as staff or collaborator with limited access, and we remove ourselves when finished. We cannot see your passwords, and we will not ask for them.
Can you promise my store cannot be hacked?
No one can promise that. We lower the common risks, such as shared logins and old access, and we give you a plain list of habits that keep the store safer.
Will you find and remove malware?
At Premium level we scan your theme and plugins for suspicious code. If a store is already infected, we tell you what we find and quote the clean-up separately.
Will this lock out my own team?
Only if you ask. We list the changes first, and we remove access only after you approve each one.

desc:
An ecommerce store security check reviews who can log in, what each account and app can do, and how your key accounts are protected. Ecom Swift LLC closes the gaps it can reach and lists the rest for you.

## What is an ecommerce store security check?

An ecommerce store security check is a review of the access and protection around your store. It looks at staff and collaborator accounts, app permissions, login settings, and the accounts that connect to the store, such as email, domain and payments. The goal is to find the easy ways in and close them.

## Why store security often fails at the basics

Most store break-ins do not involve clever hacking. They start with something ordinary: a reused password, a former employee who still has admin rights, a freelancer's access that was never removed or an app that can read far more than it needs.

The risk is practical. Someone with admin access can change prices, redirect payouts, read customer details or insert code into the checkout. Even a small store holds names, addresses and order history that visitors expect you to protect.

## How tighter access helps the business

Good access control reduces the number of places an attacker can get in. Each unused account, forgotten app or weak login is one fewer door to watch. That lowers the chance of downtime, stolen data and the loss of customer trust that follows.

It also makes the daily running of the store clearer. When every person has the access their role needs and no more, mistakes shrink. A staff member who can only manage orders cannot accidentally delete the theme. No check can promise that a store will never be attacked, but reducing exposure makes an attack harder and its damage smaller.

## What a solid security check covers

- A list of every staff, collaborator and admin account.
- Removal of old, unused and shared accounts.
- Two-step login for every admin user.
- Role and permission review for each person.
- Permissions held by each app and plugin.
- Strong login settings and protection for the admin page and forms.
- Safety review of email, domain and payment accounts, in the larger package.
- A scan of the theme for suspicious or unfamiliar code.
- Security rules for your team in writing.
- An account recovery plan.

## What we do

We start with a review of who has access. We open your user lists and compare them with the people who actually work on the store. We check whether two-step login is switched on, then review app permissions and flag any that look broader than the job requires.

Where we can safely fix a gap, we do it. That can mean removing an unused account, tightening a role, applying stronger login settings or removing a risky plugin after you approve. Where only you can act, such as turning on protection in your own email or domain account, we write step by step instructions. Standard widens the review to apps, plugins and login protection. Premium adds the domain, email and payment accounts, a theme scan for suspicious code, a written team policy and a recovery plan. We always tell you before any change that could affect how your team signs in.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Give each person their own login with the lowest role that fits.
- Turn on two-step login for every admin and email account.
- Remove access the same day someone leaves.
- Use a password manager for every shared service.
- Keep a recovery contact and backup codes in a safe place.

**Avoid:**
- Staff passing around a single store owner login.
- Keeping freelancer access open after the work ends.
- Installing apps that ask for rights they do not need.
- Sending passwords by chat or email.
- Ignoring unfamiliar sign-in alerts.

## Who this is for

This suits a store that has had several staff, freelancers or agencies over time and has lost track of who has access. It suits owners who reuse passwords across services and want a cleaner setup. It also suits a store that noticed odd behavior, such as unknown admin accounts or unexplained changes.

## What we need from you

A list of the people who should have access and what each needs to do. We work through a collaborator, staff or admin role in your account, and we do not need your passwords. For email and domain accounts, we give you instructions so you make the changes yourself.
